subject: Intermittent queue timeouts & tail-latency spike — SLA credit request
messages:
From: Jessica Hale <jessica@orionplatform.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops <ops@orionplatform.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service interruptions this morning — 504s / queue timeouts

Hi Lauren,

We saw a spike of 504s and client-side queue timeouts hitting our integration with your hosted inference API between ~08:45 and 09:05 PDT today. Affected endpoints were /v1/generate and /v1/chat for a small subset of high-concurrency routes.

Error samples attached (request ids & short traces). Our telemetry shows ~30% of requests for a 20-minute window returned 504 or timed out waiting in the client queue. This materially impacted a batch of user-facing workflows.

Can you confirm whether this aligns with anything on your side (autoscaler/backpressure/dispatch queue) and whether this would qualify for an SLA credit? We need a formal incident window and estimated credit amount for our billing team.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

— Jessica
Product Ops, Orion Platform

Hi Jessica — thanks for the report and the samples. Sorry you ran into this.

I'm escalating this to our infra and SRE team to confirm the exact window and cause. Can you confirm the earliest observed failure timestamp you have (with timezone) and whether you captured any x-request-id headers for the failing requests? That will help us map to our logs quickly.

Next steps on our side: I'll loop in infra to determine that this meets SLO breach criteria and to produce a preliminary unavailable window. We can then provide a provisional credit calc and a post-incident RCA.

I'll follow up within 24 hours with the initial timeline.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 13:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Service interruptions this morning — request for SLO window and credit calc

On Wed, Jul 22, 2026 at 10:00 AM lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — tagging you for a fast triage. Customer reports ~08:45–09:05 PDT spike of 504s/queue timeouts on hosted endpoints.

Prelim findings from infra traces and dispatch logs (us-west-2):
- Observed a tail-latency spike correlated with a transient autoscaler scheduling lag for pool "rdo-serve-prod-usw2".
- Affected requests experienced dispatch backpressure; many requests hit our per-request timeout (60s) or were dropped after queueing for >10s.
- Wall-clock impacted window we can confirm: 2026-07-22T08:46:12-07:00 -> 2026-07-22T09:02:51-07:00 (16 minutes, 39 seconds).
- Error classes: 504 gateway timeout + dispatcher-reject (queue overflow).

We've attached a filtered log bundle (orion_error_log_20260722.zip) and a short timeline (timeline_screenshot.png). Root cause: a regression in the autoscaler rollout that reduced available worker capacity for a short interval; the autoscaler recovered once replacement workers finished initialization and the backlog drained.

Credit eligibility: per our SLA, this window constitutes an availability impact. Based on Orion's monthly usage and our SLA table, preliminary credit estimate is 0.5% of monthly invoice for the impacted billing period. I'll flag this as provisional until billing/legal confirm.

Mitigations we've already applied: rollback of the autoscaler change to the previous stable rollout, tightened warm-up concurrency to avoid cold-start gaps, and a short-term dispatcher throttle to shed non-critical low-priority work during scale events.

We recommend a formal postmortem (RCA) and a follow-up call to review mitigation and permanent fixes.

— Aditya
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Hale <jessica@orionplatform.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service interruptions this morning — SLA credit & next steps

Hi Jessica — thank you for your patience. Quick update and next steps: 

1) Confirmed unavailable window: 2026-07-22T08:46:12-07:00 -> 2026-07-22T09:02:51-07:00 (16m39s) based on dispatch logs.
2) Preliminary credit: 0.5% of Orion's monthly invoice for July 2026 (provisional, pending legal/billing sign-off). We have prepared a request_for_credit_form.pdf and attached the log bundle.
3) Root cause summary (short): autoscaler rollout caused a temporary capacity gap which led to dispatcher queueing and subsequent per-request timeouts. Immediate mitigations were rolled back and throttles added.

Next steps: (a) please confirm you want us to apply the provisional credit to your July invoice (we will not finalize until billing/legal approve), and (b) would you like a formal postmortem document and a 30-minute follow-up review? We can share a full RCA with timeline, telemetry plots, and permanent mitigation plan within 5 business days.

If you confirm credit acceptance I will start the internal approvals and keep you posted.

Thanks again — we take this seriously and will work to prevent recurrence.

— Lauren
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Jessica Hale <jessica@orionplatform.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops <ops@orionplatform.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service interruptions this morning — SLA credit & next steps

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the transparency — the timeline and attachments look good. We accept the provisional credit and would like the formal postmortem and a 30-minute review focused on the autoscaler rollout safeguards.

Two asks for the RCA: please include (1) the exact autoscaler change that triggered the reduction in warm capacity, (2) why the warm-up concurrency did not prevent the gap, and (3) proposed guardrails for future rollouts (feature-flagged rollout, canary for autoscaler, increased observability on queue length).

We'll consider the credit final once we receive the postmortem and confirm the mitigation plan. Please let us know available slots for next week.

— Jessica
Product Ops, Orion Platform
